newsitem.title: GHANA: U.N.'s Annan urges Africa to pull together.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Annan urges Africa to pull together.

text.p: Incoming U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan returned home to Ghana for the Christmas break on Friday and urged Africa to pull together to solve its problems.

Annan, formally appointed by the U.N. General Assembly on Wednesday, said he would try to focus the attention of member states on Africa's problems but added that political stability was essential if the region was to attract foreign investors.
"We have a challenge to solve our problems. If we pull in the right direction, it will be done," he told reporters.
Annan, who arrived with his Swedish wife and step-daughter for a week's holiday, said he aimed to make the U.N. more relevant in world affairs "as we move into the 21st century".
He pledged to continue the reform process launched by his predecessor, Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali, whose mandate expires at the end of the year.
He said that he favoured extending permanent seats on the Security Council to Germany and Japan but also to countries in other regions.

U.N. officials said the visit was intended to be as private as possible. Annan was due to have talks with President Jerry Rawlings, who this month made history by becoming the first incumbent to win reelection since independence in 1957.
